goal: Open the year by asking which questions describe every function met so far, sort a set of function family cards, then bring back shifts, stretches, reflections and even and odd symmetry.
note: Base OSP 1.1 and 1.5 (merged). Hook, then the review half-day (25 minutes toward the 15 percent cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-transformations-functions. Unit 1 has no readiness rows (every assumed row is retrieval), so day 1 holds no readiness check.

goal: Read domain and range from graphs and situations again, then write them in interval notation, including the pieces of a piecewise rule.
note: Base OSP 1.2. Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg1-domain-range. Interval notation is the unit's one new tool; piecewise domains are the language Calculus uses for continuity.

goal: Find where a function rises and falls and locate its turning points, written with intervals.
note: Base OSP 1.3 in part (increasing, decreasing and extrema; the average rate of change waits for unit 10).

goal: Decide algebraically whether a function is even, odd or neither, describe end behavior in words and arrows, and read an absolute value function as a piecewise rule.
note: Base OSP 1.5 and 1.6 (merged). End behavior stays in words and arrows; limit notation waits for unit 10.

goal: Analyze unfamiliar functions from every family met so far with the same set of questions and argue which family fits a graph, a table or a description.
note: Mixed set across the families; the exit ticket gives a family not yet analyzed this week.

goal: Build f(g(x)) from two formulas and from two tables, and evaluate it at given inputs.
note: Base OSP 1.4. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-combining-functions-models and alg1-function-notation.

goal: Evaluate a composition from two graphs and find the domain of a composite function.
note: Base OSP 1.4.

goal: Write a situation as a composition, temperature as a function of altitude and altitude as a function of time, and interpret the composite.
note: Base OSP 1.4 contexts, our data. Sensitivity: the altitude and temperature values come from the international standard atmosphere table, said to be a model, not a measurement. Extension kept (10 minutes): a chain of three functions, shown once.

goal: Split a given function into an inner and an outer function in more than one way and check each split by composing.
note: Base OSP 1.4. The inner and outer split is the move the chain rule uses in Calculus.

goal: Verify by composing in both orders that two functions are inverses.
note: Base OSP 1.7. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg1-inverse-functions (the linear case) and alg2-rational-exponents (the cube root as the inverse of cubing).

goal: Read values of an inverse from the graph or table of an invertible function, and draw a function and its inverse on one grid with the line y = x.
note: Base OSP 1.7. Extension kept inside the day: the function, its inverse and y = x on one grid.

goal: Make squaring invertible by restricting its domain, use the horizontal line test, and give the square root as the inverse on that domain.
note: Base OSP 3.8 and 1.7 (merged): the domain restriction that unit 3 and unit 4 reuse.

goal: Restrict the domains of other functions (an absolute value, a quadratic in vertex form, a linear-over-linear rational) so each has an inverse, and verify each inverse by composition.
note: Base OSP 3.8. Mixed set; inverses of rational functions stay linear over linear.

goal: Practice the unit's moves on a mixed set: interval notation, symmetry, compositions from formulas, tables and graphs, and inverses with restricted domains.
note: Practice of days 1 to 13 only.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: analyze functions, compose and decompose them, and verify, read and build inverses on unseen items.
note: One sitting of unseen items, a prompt for each part of each code (4b, 4c and 4d each their own). Response on day 16, counted once.

goal: Act on the assessment: regroup by the items missed, rework them with the earlier model, and retry a parallel item alone.
note: Planned for 30 students in parallel groups; no serial one-to-one retesting. Unit 2 has no readiness rows.

goal: Open the unit by asking how we can be sure every zero is found, bring back complex arithmetic and quadratics with complex solutions, then divide complex numbers with the conjugate and find a modulus.
note: Base OSP 3.1 (merged into the review). Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-complex-numbers and alg2-quadratics-complex-solutions. Division by the conjugate is the new part.

goal: Bring back polynomial division and the Remainder Theorem, add synthetic division as a shortcut, and recall how end behavior and multiplicity shape a polynomial graph.
note: Base OSP 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 (merged). Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-polynomial-division-remainder.

goal: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers and factor sums of squares such as x squared + 4 = (x + 2i)(x - 2i).
note: Base OSP 3.6 in part.

goal: State the fundamental theorem of algebra and show it holds for every quadratic by completing the square.
note: Base OSP 3.6. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg1-completing-square (a quadratic put in vertex form), which the day then uses; completing the square stays in the openings from here.

goal: Find the real zeros of a cubic with integer coefficients from rational candidates and the factor theorem.
note: Base OSP 3.6.

goal: Use conjugate pairs to find every zero of a quartic, real and complex, and write it as a product of linear factors.
note: Base OSP 3.6.

goal: Practice finding every zero of degree 3 and 4 polynomials and writing each as a product of linear factors, checked against a graph.
note: Base OSP 3.6 practice. Extension kept (15 minutes, optional): a degree 5 polynomial with a given graph, every zero found.

goal: Compare rational expressions with rational numbers, multiply and divide them, and state the nonzero restriction on each divisor.
note: Review half-day (25 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-rational-equations (simplifying and solving with each step explained). The system view of rational expressions is ours; the base text has no section for it.

goal: Add and subtract rational expressions with unlike denominators and argue that the set is closed under all four operations by a nonzero divisor.
note: Ours. Adding rational expressions is how Calculus checks a partial-fraction split.

goal: Practice rewriting rational expressions with all four operations and naming the restrictions.
note: Practice of days 24 and 25; this fluency stays in the openings all year.

goal: Graph rational functions with vertical and horizontal asymptotes and a hole as in Algebra II, then read each feature from the factored form.
note: Base OSP 3.7. Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-rational-functions.

goal: Find slant asymptotes by division and read a rational function fully from its factored form, its sign on each interval included.
note: Base OSP 3.7. Review half-day (25 minutes toward the cap): the sign of each interval checked against Algebra II graphs.

goal: Solve polynomial inequalities with a sign chart on the number line and check the answer on a graph.
note: Ours (the base text has no sign-chart section). Number-line model.

goal: Solve rational inequalities with a sign chart, including one from a cost-per-item situation, and explain why the excluded values matter.
note: Ours. Extension kept inside the day: the cost-per-item inequality (invented for practice, labeled so).

goal: End-of-unit assessment: complex division, complex factoring, every zero of a polynomial, rational expressions and rational inequalities on unseen items.
codes: N-CN.A.3; N-CN.C.8; N-CN.C.9; CUR-PC.2; A-APR.D.7; CUR-PC.3
note: One sitting; a prompt for each part of each code (N-CN.C.9: the theorem stated and shown for a quadratic). Response on day 32, counted once.

goal: Act on the assessment in groups, rework missed items with the earlier model, and retry a parallel item alone.
codes: N-CN.A.3; N-CN.C.8; N-CN.C.9; CUR-PC.2; A-APR.D.7; CUR-PC.3
note: Planned for 30 students. Unit 3 has no readiness rows.

goal: Open the unit by asking which model fits a set of growth data, bring back exponential graphs and logarithms as solutions, then meet the logarithm as the inverse of the exponential with the same base.
note: Base OSP 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 (merged). Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-logarithms and alg2-exp-log-graphs.

goal: Check by composing that a logarithm and its exponential undo each other, the natural logarithm and e to the x included, and graph a logarithm as the reflection of its exponential in y = x.
note: Base OSP 4.3 and 4.4. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-number-e-continuous (e as the limit of compounding more often), so ln meets a familiar e. Unit 1's inverses carry the idea; ln as the inverse of e to the x is what Calculus picks up.

goal: Derive the product, quotient and power properties of logarithms from the exponent rules and use them to rewrite.
note: Base OSP 4.5.

goal: Derive the change of base formula and use it to evaluate and compare logarithms.
note: Base OSP 4.5.

goal: Practice expanding, condensing and changing the base of logarithmic expressions.
note: Practice of days 35 and 36; untimed, and kept in the openings all year.

goal: Solve exponential and logarithmic equations exactly and reject any candidate outside the domain.
note: Base OSP 4.6.

goal: Apply continuous growth with e and bring back exponential rules from two points, then model half-life and doubling time and solve for the time.
note: Base OSP 4.7. Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-exponential-growth-rational-inputs; e itself was retrieved in day 34's opening and is applied here. Sensitivity: carbon dating with a half-life of about 5,730 years; no illness or drug-dose context. Chemistry's half-life (grade 10) named as a second context.

goal: Use logarithmic scales, sound level in decibels and the brightness of named stars, and explain what a step of one on each scale means.
note: Base OSP 4.7. Star magnitudes from a public catalogue page, as of the date read.

goal: Straighten curved data by taking logarithms of one variable (semi-log) or both (log-log, planets' periods and distances), fit a line by eye or with technology, and read the model back.
note: Base OSP 4.8, plus the straightening on semi-log paper (ours). Extension kept as the log-log case. Paired devices; paper path: semi-log paper and a printed residual table.

goal: Read a logistic model for its carrying capacity, midpoint and growth rate, and fit one on paper by straightening ln(y / (L - y)) against time.
note: Base OSP 4.7 (logistic part). Lean retrieval (Biology, grade 9, carrying capacity): if a student has not met it, the day names carrying capacity as the level the counts approach. Logistic models are read and fitted, not derived.

goal: Modeling task: take published wolf counts through assumptions, model choice, fitting, interpretation and validation, and draft a short report on how far the model can be trusted.
note: Ours. The full modeling cycle; the teacher's written feedback returns on day 46. Sensitivity: wildlife counts given in full (Yellowstone gray wolves 1995 to 2004, the unit plan checks the logistic fit before keeping the pick; the next pick is household internet access); no disease-spread context.

goal: Practice a mixed set of logarithm rules, exact equations and model readings across the unit.
note: Practice of days 33 to 42.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: logarithms as inverses, the properties, exact equations and growth models on unseen items.
note: One sitting; a prompt for each part of each code. The modeling report is scored on our rubric after its revision, not here. Response on day 46, counted once.

goal: Act on the assessment in groups, then revise the wolf-count report from the written feedback, testing the model against one more year of counts.
note: First 25 minutes: response to the sitting, counted once. Last 25 minutes: report revision (the cycle's revision and report steps; extension kept: one more year of counts). The report is scored after this day. Unit 4's readiness check sits on day 49.

goal: Check 1, audit and repair: an audit-and-repair set: worked solutions with errors to find, explain and correct, and "which method and why" items, fresh cases on function analysis, composition and inverses, complex zeros and sign charts from units 1 and 2.
codes: CUR-PC.1; F-BF.A.1c; F-BF.B.4b; F-BF.B.4d; N-CN.A.3; CUR-PC.2; A-APR.D.7; CUR-PC.3
note: Course-level check right after unit 3's end: it draws no items on unit 3; unit 3's record from day 45 is reused unscored with its date. A different task form from day 45's unseen items. Parts sampled: CUR-PC.1, symmetry and end behavior; F-BF.B.4d, an inverse by restricting the domain; N-CN.A.3, quotients by the conjugate; CUR-PC.2, every zero of a quartic; A-APR.D.7, adding with unlike denominators; CUR-PC.3, a rational inequality by sign chart. Each item names its code and the next step for a student who misses it.

goal: Check 1, extended task: one multi-step task joining units 1 and 2, a composed rational function analyzed for its domain, zeros and sign, with a written explanation.
note: One extended task only; a different task form from day 47 and from day 45.

goal: Respond to check 1 by group: reteach from the item analysis and retry parallel items; then unit 4's readiness check.
note: First 40 minutes: response by group, planned for 30 students. Last 10 minutes: unit 4's readiness check on geo-solving-right-triangles (last used grade 10, Geometry unit 4); results shape day 50, and misses get a reminder with the earlier model in the openings of days 50 to 52.

goal: Open the unit by asking how a sine can be known exactly, bring back radians and the unit circle, then find exact values at pi/6, pi/4 and pi/3 from the two special triangles.
note: Base OSP 5.1 and 5.4 (merged into the review), 5.2. Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-unit-circle-radians and geo-right-triangle-trig. Readiness misses from day 49 get their reminder in the opening.

goal: Use reference angles and the symmetries pi minus x, pi plus x and 2pi minus x to find exact values at every multiple of the special angles, and write sin, cos and tan of pi minus x, pi plus x and 2pi minus x in terms of their values at x for any real x, checked at a non-special angle on the calculator.
note: Base OSP 5.2.

goal: Explain with the unit circle why sine and tangent are odd, cosine is even, sine and cosine repeat every 2pi and tangent every pi.
note: Base OSP 5.3 in part.

goal: Practice exact sine, cosine and tangent values at the special angles and their multiples all around the circle.
note: Practice of days 50 to 52; untimed, and kept in the openings all year.

goal: Find all six trigonometric values from the unit circle, with secant, cosecant and cotangent as reciprocals.
note: Base OSP 5.3.

goal: Bring back sine and cosine graphs with amplitude, midline and period, then add the phase shift as its own move.
note: Base OSP 6.1. Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-trig-functions-graphs.

goal: Write a sine or cosine rule from a graph with all four parameters, and give a sound wave's frequency as one over its period.
note: Base OSP 6.1. Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-trig-functions-graphs (writing rules from graphs). Lean retrieval (Physics, grade 11, wave math): if not met, the day names frequency as one over the period and gives the wave's graph.

goal: Graph tangent and cotangent with their asymptotes and periods.
note: Base OSP 6.2.

goal: Graph secant and cosecant from the cosine and sine graphs they are reciprocals of.
note: Base OSP 6.2. All six graphs are what Calculus differentiates.

goal: Practice sketching all six trigonometric graphs from rules and writing rules from graphs.
note: Practice of days 54 to 58.

goal: Restrict sine, cosine and tangent to intervals where each always rises or always falls so each has an inverse, as unit 1 restricted squaring.
note: Base OSP 6.3.

goal: Evaluate inverse sine, cosine and tangent from the unit circle and with a calculator, and compare the calculator's one answer with the unit circle's two.
note: Base OSP 6.3. Extension kept inside the day: inverse cosine on the calculator against the unit circle. Readiness results from day 49 used for angles from right triangles.

goal: Solve a trigonometric equation from a periodic model with an inverse function and say what each answer means in context.
note: Base OSP 7.6 in part (split with unit 5). Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-periodic-modeling.

goal: Tide task: through a compact modeling cycle, find when the tide at one coastal station first reaches a given height and check the answer against the tide table.
note: Ours (the compact cycle: assumptions, model, solve with an inverse, interpret, check). Sensitivity: tide predictions for one named station, said to be predictions, as of the year read.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: exact values, symmetry, the six functions and their graphs, and inverse trigonometric functions in context on unseen items.
note: One sitting; a prompt for each part of each code (F-TF.A.3: values from the special triangles, and the general symmetry for any real x; F-TF.A.4: odd and even, and periodicity, tangent included; F-TF.B.7: solve, evaluate with technology, interpret). Response on day 65, counted once.

goal: Act on the assessment in groups, rework missed items with the unit circle, and retry a parallel item alone.
note: Planned for 30 students. Unit 5 has no readiness rows.

goal: Open the unit by asking how we can prove two expressions are always equal, and prove simple identities by a chain of equal expressions, one side rewritten into the other.
note: Base OSP 7.1. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-pythagorean-identity. A graph of both sides checks a claim and is never a proof; never operate on both sides of an identity as if it were known true.

goal: Prove the cosine subtraction and addition formulas from the distance between two points on the unit circle.
note: Base OSP 7.2.

goal: Derive the sine and tangent addition and subtraction formulas from the cosine formula and find exact values such as sin 75 degrees.
note: Base OSP 7.2.

goal: Practice exact values and rewriting with the addition and subtraction formulas.
note: Practice of days 67 and 68.

goal: Derive the double-angle formulas from the addition formulas and use them in proofs.
note: Base OSP 7.3.

goal: Derive the power-reducing formulas from the double-angle formulas, then the half-angle formulas, and use them for exact values.
note: Base OSP 7.3. The power-reducing forms are what Calculus uses for polar area.

goal: Prove new identities built from the proved ones, choosing which side to rewrite or rewriting each side to the same expression.
note: Base OSP 7.1 and 7.3 practice. Extension kept (15 minutes, optional): the product-to-sum formulas derived from the addition formulas.

goal: Solve trigonometric equations exactly at the special angles, giving every solution in a stated interval and the general solution with its period.
note: Base OSP 7.5.

goal: Solve trigonometric equations that need factoring or an identity first, such as a quadratic in sine or an equation with a double angle.
note: Base OSP 7.1 and 7.5 (merged).

goal: Solve trigonometric equations with a calculator where no special angle fits, using symmetry to find every solution in the interval.
note: Base OSP 7.5. Solving sin x = c on an interval is what Calculus retrieves for extrema.

goal: Practice rewriting with the Pythagorean, addition and double-angle forms and solving equations in an interval.
note: Practice of days 66 to 75; untimed, and kept in the openings all year.

goal: Solve equations from a daylight model and a pure tone's sound wave to answer when a given value is reached, and interpret each solution.
note: Base OSP 7.6 in part. The sound wave is invented for practice from a stated frequency, labeled so.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: addition formulas proved and used, identities proved by a chain, and equations solved in an interval and in general on unseen items.
note: One sitting; a prompt for each part of each code (F-TF.C.9: prove and use). Response on day 79, counted once.

goal: Act on the assessment in groups, repair broken proof chains and missing solutions, and retry a parallel item alone.
note: Planned for 30 students. Unit 6 has no readiness rows (its geometry rows were used in unit 4).

goal: Open the unit by asking how to find a distance we cannot measure, bring back right-triangle trigonometry, then derive the area formula one half ab sin C by drawing an altitude.
note: Base OSP 8.1 (area). Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): geo-solving-right-triangles (used in unit 4 this year) and geo-right-triangle-trig.

goal: Prove the law of sines from two altitudes and use it to solve triangles given two angles and a side.
note: Base OSP 8.1.

goal: Find the zero, one or two triangles that two sides and a non-included angle allow, by drawing and with the law of sines.
note: Base OSP 8.1 (the ambiguous case).

goal: Prove the law of cosines with coordinates and use it to solve triangles given two sides and the included angle or all three sides.
note: Base OSP 8.2.

goal: Survey a triangular lot and find the distance to a lighthouse, choosing the law each case needs and checking the answer by a second route.
note: Base OSP 8.1 and 8.2 contexts, our values (invented for practice, labeled so). Extension kept (15 minutes, optional): Heron's formula from the law of cosines.

goal: End-of-unit assessment, triangle sitting: the area formula, the laws of sines and cosines proved and used, and the ambiguous case on unseen items.
note: The first of unit 6's two sittings (frame). Written feedback is handed back on day 87; the response is on day 98 with the vector sitting's, counted once.

goal: Treat a vector as a quantity with magnitude and direction, drawn as a directed segment and written v, |v| and ||v||, and read Geometry's translation rules as vectors.
note: Base OSP 8.8. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): geo-transformations-coordinates. The vector-arrow model starts here.

goal: Find a vector's components by subtracting the initial point from the terminal point, and its magnitude and direction from the components.
note: Base OSP 8.8.

goal: Add vectors end to end, by components and by the parallelogram rule, and explain why the magnitude of a sum is usually less than the sum of the magnitudes.
note: Base OSP 8.8.

goal: Find the magnitude and direction of a sum from the magnitudes and directions of its parts with the law of cosines.
note: Base OSP 8.8. The law of cosines from days 83 and 84 returns as the way a resultant's length is found. The opening is drawn from day 85's most-missed law-of-cosines items (written feedback goes back on day 87); practice, never check evidence.

goal: Subtract vectors as adding the additive inverse, drawn and by components.
note: Base OSP 8.8. With days 88 and 89 this completes the parent N-VM.B.4.

goal: Multiply a vector by a scalar, drawn and by components, and say what happens to its magnitude and direction, a negative scalar included.
note: Base OSP 8.8.

goal: Solve velocity and force problems with vectors: a plane in a crosswind and three forces holding a hanging sign in balance.
note: Base OSP 8.8 contexts, our values. Lean retrieval (Physics, grade 11, net force): if not met, force is treated as a vector with given magnitude and direction and only the net force is asked. Extension kept inside the day: three forces in balance. Sensitivity: planes and signs only, no military context.

goal: Modeling task: plan a boat's crossing of a river with a current, from assumptions through the vector model, computation and interpretation, and draft the report.
note: Ours. The full modeling cycle; written feedback returns on day 96. Values invented for practice, labeled so; no military context.

goal: Find the dot product, the angle between two vectors and whether two vectors are perpendicular.
note: Base OSP 8.8 (dot product).

goal: Project one vector onto another and use the dot product to find the work a force does along a path.
note: Ours (the base text has no projection).

goal: Revise the boat-crossing report from the written feedback, validating the plan against a changed current, then work a mixed set of vector problems.
note: First 25 minutes: report revision (the cycle's validation, revision and report steps); the report is scored after this day. Then mixed practice of days 86 to 95.

goal: End-of-unit assessment, vector sitting: vectors, components, sums and differences, scalar multiples, applications and the dot product on unseen items.
codes: N-VM.A.1; N-VM.A.2; N-VM.B.4; N-VM.B.4a; N-VM.B.4b; N-VM.B.4c; N-VM.A.3; N-VM.B.5; N-VM.B.5a; N-VM.B.5b; CUR-PC.9
note: The second sitting; a prompt for each lettered part (4a, 4b, 4c, 5a, 5b). Response on day 98, counted once.

goal: Act on both sittings in groups, triangles and vectors, rework missed items with the vector-arrow model, and retry a parallel item alone.
note: Planned for 30 students; one response for both sittings, counted once. Unit 7's readiness check sits on day 101.

goal: Check 2, audit and repair: an audit-and-repair set: worked solutions with errors to find, explain and correct, and "which method and why" items, fresh cases from units 1 to 5, weighted to exact values, trigonometric graphs, inverses, identities and equations.
codes: F-BF.B.4d; CUR-PC.4; F-TF.A.3; F-TF.A.4; CUR-PC.6; F-TF.B.6; F-TF.C.9; CUR-PC.7; CUR-PC.8
note: Course-level check right after unit 6's end: it draws no items on unit 6; unit 6's record from days 85 and 97 is reused unscored with its dates. A different task form from day 97's unseen items. Parts sampled: CUR-PC.4, change of base and an exact equation with a rejected candidate; F-TF.A.3, the general symmetry for any real x; F-TF.A.4, odd and even with tangent's period; CUR-PC.6, secant and cosecant graphs and a rule from a graph; F-TF.C.9, use; CUR-PC.7, a chain proof with a double-angle formula; CUR-PC.8, every solution in a stated interval. Each item names its code and the next step for a student who misses it.

goal: Check 2, extended task: a periodic model from units 4 and 5 solved with an identity and an inverse function, every solution in the interval interpreted.
note: One extended task only; a different task form from day 99 and from day 97.

goal: Respond to check 2 by group, retry parallel items, then unit 7's readiness check.
note: First 40 minutes: response by group, planned for 30 students. Last 10 minutes: unit 7's readiness check on geo-rigid-motion-definitions, geo-dilations and alg1-linear-systems (each last used grade 10); results shape day 102, misses get a reminder with the earlier model in the openings of days 102 to 104 and on day 110.

goal: Open the unit by asking how one array can hold a network, move a shape or solve a system; hold a bus network and a league table in matrices, then add, subtract and multiply by a scalar.
note: Base OSP 9.5. The matrix model starts here. Sensitivity: the league table scores points, never bets or payouts; the network and table are invented for practice, labeled so.

goal: Multiply matrices of fitting dimensions and read what a product of a network matrix with itself counts.
note: Base OSP 9.5.

goal: Test whether matrix multiplication is associative, distributive and commutative, and find the zero and identity matrices.
note: Base OSP 9.5.

goal: Find the determinant and inverse of a 2 by 2 matrix and explain why an inverse exists exactly when the determinant is not zero.
note: Base OSP 9.7 in part.

goal: Modeling task: rank the connections of a small bus network by matrix powers, state the assumptions, interpret the counts and draft the report.
note: Ours. The full modeling cycle; written feedback returns on day 112. Paired devices for the matrix powers; paper path: 3 by 3 products by hand.

goal: Multiply a vector by a matrix to get a new vector and treat the matrix as a transformation of vectors.
note: Ours (the base text has no section). Readiness results from day 101 used: transformations as functions on points.

goal: Use 2 by 2 matrices to rotate, reflect, dilate and stretch the plane, and read the absolute value of the determinant as the factor by which areas change.
note: Ours. Geometry's rigid motions and dilations return as matrices.

goal: Compose transformations as matrix products, comparing a 30 degree rotation applied twice with a 60 degree rotation, and predict an image's area.
note: Ours. Extension kept inside the day: the two rotations compared, set up for unit 8's complex multiplication.

goal: Bring back linear systems from Algebra I, then write a system of linear equations as one matrix equation.
note: Base OSP 9.2 (merged). Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg1-linear-systems, checked on day 101 as readiness. A zero determinant tied back to systems with no or many solutions.

goal: Solve a matrix equation with the inverse of its coefficient matrix, a 2 by 2 by hand and a 3 by 3 with technology; read the tool's 3 by 3 determinant and see that a zero determinant leaves no inverse.
note: Base OSP 9.7. Paired devices for the 3 by 3 inverse (A-REI.C.9 needs technology); a student on the paper path enters the matrix on a shared device or in a scheduled device session, never a given inverse alone.

goal: Revise the bus-network report from the written feedback, then set up and solve a 3 by 3 mixture system with technology.

goal: Open the unit by asking what curves appear when a point is named by a distance and an angle; locate points with polar coordinates and explain why one point has many polar names.

goal: Turn a polar point into x and y with the unit circle and back with the angle's quadrant, then rewrite r = 4 cos theta as a circle's equation.
note: Base OSP 8.3.

goal: Practice moving points and curves between the two grids.

goal: Sketch polar circles and lines from a table of values and test each for symmetry.

goal: Sketch cardioids and other limacons from a table, symmetry and the largest and smallest radius.

goal: Sketch rose curves and spirals, and predict the number of petals from the equation.
note: Base OSP 8.4.

goal: Match polar equations to graphs and justify each match, and find where two polar curves meet by solving a trigonometric equation.
note: Base OSP 8.4 practice. Joins units 5 and 8; the meeting points are what Calculus needs for the area between polar curves.

goal: Plot complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form and explain why both name the same number.
note: Base OSP 8.5. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-complex-numbers (and unit 2's conjugate and modulus).

goal: Show addition, subtraction and conjugation of complex numbers as arrows on the complex plane.
note: Base OSP 8.5. Unit 6's vector-arrow model returns.

goal: Multiply complex numbers in polar form by multiplying moduli and adding arguments, compute (-1 + root 3 i) cubed, and compare with unit 7's rotation matrix.
note: Base OSP 8.5 (powers; roots are an extension only). Extension kept (10 minutes, optional): the cube roots of 8 on the complex plane.

goal: Find the distance between two complex numbers as the modulus of their difference and the midpoint as the average of the endpoints.
note: Ours (the base text has no section for N-CN.B.6).

goal: Graph a curve given by parametric equations from a table of t values, showing the direction of travel.
note: Base OSP 8.6. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-unit-circle-radians: (cos t, sin t) as a moving point.

goal: Eliminate the parameter where possible and write parametric equations for a line segment and a circle.
note: Base OSP 8.6 and 8.7.

goal: Modeling task: write a thrown ball's path parametrically from its launch speed and angle, check it against a table of positions, and draft the report.
note: Base OSP 8.7 context; the task is ours. The full modeling cycle; written feedback returns on day 130. goal: Practice graphing parametric curves with direction, eliminating the parameter and converting polar equations.
note: Practice of days 115 to 128.

goal: Revise the thrown-ball report from the written feedback, then work a mixed set joining polar curves, complex numbers and parametric motion.
note: First 25 minutes: report revision (validation, revision, report); scored after this day.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: polar coordinates and graphs, complex numbers in polar form, and parametric curves on unseen items.

goal: Open the unit by asking why an orbit, a dish and a whispering gallery share a family of curves; bring back the circle and parabola equations and completing the square, and name the circle as the first conic.
note: Base OSP 10.3 in part. Review day (50 minutes toward the cap): Retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a student who misses it gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): geo-circle-parabola-equations and alg1-completing-square.

goal: Construct a perpendicular at a point as a warm-up, then construct the tangent from a point outside a circle and justify it by the right angle between radius and tangent.
note: Ours (the base text has no section for G-C.A.4). Construction comes back with one familiar construction first.

goal: Confirm the constructed tangent with coordinates, showing the radius and tangent slopes are perpendicular, and write the tangent lines' equations.
note: Ours. The circle's tangent is what Calculus calls back in implicit differentiation.

goal: Derive the equation of an ellipse from the constant sum of distances to its foci.
note: Base OSP 10.1. Extension kept (15 minutes): an ellipse drawn with two pins and a loop of string, the sum of distances made visible.

goal: Write and graph ellipses in standard form from their features, model a planet's orbit from its nearest and farthest distances, and link (cos t, sin t) to (a cos t, b sin t).
note: Base OSP 10.1. Lean retrieval (Physics, grade 11, orbits): if not met, the day gives the distances at nearest and farthest approach and builds the ellipse from them. Planetary distances from a public fact sheet, as of the date read.

goal: Derive the equation of a hyperbola from the constant difference of distances to its foci.
note: Base OSP 10.2.

goal: Write and graph hyperbolas in standard form with their asymptotes, and locate a ship from the time difference of two shore signals.
note: Base OSP 10.2. Extension kept inside the day: the ship. Sensitivity: ships at sea only, no military use.

goal: Write parabolas in standard form from focus and directrix, then put a general second-degree equation with no xy term in standard form by completing the square and name its conic.
note: Base OSP 10.3.

goal: Practice putting general second-degree equations in standard form, naming each conic and sketching it from its features.
note: Practice of days 133 to 140; completing the square stays in the openings.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: ellipse and hyperbola equations derived from their foci, conics in standard form, and the tangent construction justified on unseen items.
note: One sitting; a prompt for each part of each code (G-C.A.4: construct and justify). Response on day 143, counted once.

goal: Act on the assessment in groups and retry a parallel item alone.
note: Planned for 30 students. Unit 10 has no readiness rows.

goal: Open the unit by asking how adding forever can give a finite answer; bring back sequences and the finite geometric sum, then write sums in sigma notation.

goal: Find the sum of an infinite geometric series with ratio between -1 and 1 from its partial sums, a bouncing ball's total distance included, and explain why other ratios give no finite sum.
note: Base OSP 11.4. Extension kept (10 minutes): 0.999... as a geometric series. The bouncing ball is invented for practice, labeled so.

goal: Compare partial-sum tables of 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... and 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 + ... and see that one grows without bound and one does not.
note: Ours. Calculus tells such series apart; here they are only seen. Paper path: a printed partial-sum table.

goal: Expand (x + y) to the n with the binomial theorem, coefficients from Pascal's triangle and counted as combinations.
note: Base OSP 11.5 in part and 11.6. Five-minute opening is the retrieval task (practice, never check evidence; a miss gets a brief reminder with the earlier model): alg2-polynomial-arithmetic. Combinations are a bridge here, just enough to count the coefficients; Statistics owns counting (S-CP.B.9) and it is not claimed.

goal: Find a chosen term of a binomial expansion and expand binomials with coefficients and negative terms, then mix in series problems.
note: Base OSP 11.6 practice.

goal: Find the average rate of change over shorter and shorter intervals and draw the secant lines.

note: Base OSP 12.4 in part (secant slopes; derivative notation and rules left to Calculus).

goal: Estimate the instantaneous rate of cooling from a table of temperatures and explain how the estimate improves as the interval shrinks.

goal: Describe the value a function approaches as the input nears a number, from both sides, with tables and graphs.

goal: Describe behavior at a hole, near a vertical asymptote and as the input grows without bound, and read e and an infinite sum as values approached.
note: Base OSP 12.1. No formal definition and no limit laws.
